title: processkit-cli `cancel`/`kill` acknowledgement and `--all` report
description: The machine-readable stdout of the mutating control-plane commands, in both forms: the single-target acknowledgement (`cancel --run-id <id>` / `kill --run-id <id>`, one JSON object — the runner's own reply line, printed verbatim once the client has verified it) and the aggregate report (`cancel --all` / `kill --all`, one JSON array with one entry per snapshot target). Validate against `#/$defs/ack` or `#/$defs/controlAllReport` directly when the invocation is known. The normative prose is docs/control-plane.md, "The ack" and "`cancel --all` / `kill --all`"; the in-code source of truth is src/control/mod.rs. Validated against fixtures/schema/cli/control-ack.jsonl, and against the real binary's output, by tests/machine_output.rs.

ack.description: The single-target acknowledgement: the runner accepted the command and began tearing the run down. This is the one shape published here that also crosses a process boundary (runner to client) and it still carries no version field — see fixtures/schema/cli/README.md, "Versioning".

accepted.description: Always true in printed output: the client verifies `accepted`/`action`/`run_id` against the command it sent and fails closed with CONTROL (103) on any mismatch, so a rejected or garbled reply is never printed as a false success.

action.description: The action taken, echoed so the client can confirm the runner answered the verb it sent.

run_id.description: The run the command targeted — the id the client matched in the registry.

controlAllReport.description: `cancel --all` / `kill --all`'s report: exactly one entry per target in the registry snapshot taken when the invocation started — no entry is ever skipped silently. An empty confirmed-live snapshot prints `[]` and exits 0; any `failed` entry makes the whole command exit CONTROL (103) *after* printing the complete report, never a silent 0 on partial failure.

run_id.description: The target record's run id. Descriptive only: aggregate dispatch is keyed by the unique registry-record path, so two live records sharing an id are still addressed independently.

accepted.description: Whether a live runner acknowledged this invocation's mutation.

status.description: `accepted` — the runner acknowledged the verb; `already_gone` — the target finished before its turn, so the desired terminal state is already reached without an ack (successful, not an error); `failed` — the still-potentially-live target could not be safely reached or did not acknowledge.

error.description: Why a `failed` target was not accepted; null for both successful statuses.
